assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishes a new physical-chemical concept of cellular organisation: membraneless compartments forming by liquid-liquid demixing of multivalent biomolecules, governed by phase behaviour, valency and interaction strength. It reduces a messy cell-biological phenomenon to general thermodynamic principles, which is exactly the kind of concept-level contribution I value, and it has reshaped how chemists and biologists think about intracellular organisation, disease aggregation and amyloid-like transitions.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed the liquid-like behaviour of P granules and nucleoli, and Rosen's multivalent-interaction work supplied the quantitative phase-separation framework. Pappu and Mittag made decisive theoretical and sequence-grammar contributions, so the three-person cut leaves out important people, and I am not independently certain how the community would split credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in many systems and in vitro reconstitutions, and the field is large and still growing. The physical principle is solid, but how far condensates function as such in living cells (versus in vitro behaviour or artefacts of overexpression) is still contested, so part of the field is arguably not yet settled.
uncertainties: Physiological relevance of phase separation in vivo is debated and some claims rest on overexpression
Allocation of credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is unresolved
Whether this is chemistry or cell biology for prize-field purposes

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Lipid self-assembly applied to a transformative problem: ionizable cationic lipids that are neutral in circulation and charged in the endosome, formulated into nanoparticles that encapsulate nucleic acids. This is lipid phase behaviour, pKa-tuned charge and membrane fusion principles turned into a technology that enabled siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines at global scale. The impact is exceptionally clear, and it is physical chemistry of lipids at its best.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group carried out the foundational lipid-nanoparticle and ionizable-lipid work, with Madden and Hope central in the early formulation and loading methods. Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan also contributed meaningfully (lipid libraries, SNALP clinical translation), and the credit is split between academic and company work, so a fair three-person configuration is arguable but not clean.
assessment.maturity: Strong, independent validation through approved siRNA and mRNA products and the widespread clinical use. Timing is highly appropriate. The mRNA nucleoside-modification work was already recognised in Medicine, so an overlap-with-prior-prize question exists but the delivery chemistry is distinct.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Cullis, Madden, Hope, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA vaccines
Patent and company history complicates attribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics introduced a unified, tractable scheme for ab initio dynamics, so that bond making and breaking, solvation, water structure and phase behaviour could be simulated from electronic structure. It became a foundation for computational condensed-phase chemistry and a basis for ab initio treatment of liquids, interfaces and reactions, a field I follow closely as a physical chemist.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is unusually clean: the 1985 paper is by Car and Parrinello and the credit is shared essentially exclusively by these two. A two-person prize is straightforward.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of validation and universal adoption in chemistry, physics and materials science, so recognition is, if anything, overdue. Parrinello also appears in metadynamics and machine-learned potentials, which could complicate how his contributions are bundled.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to recognise Parrinello for this or for later work on metadynamics and machine-learned potentials
Computational methods have been recognised in 2013 and 2024, so some committee members may view the area as recently rewarded

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly of discrete cages and polyhedra showed that thermodynamically controlled, reversible coordination can build complex, well-defined molecular architectures from simple components, an elegant case of self-assembly principles in molecular chemistry. It enabled confined-space chemistry, host-guest behaviour, catalysis in cavities and molecular recognition.
assessment.attribution: Fujita (self-assembled coordination cages and the M6L4 cage), Raymond (coordination-driven tetrahedral cages and catalysis in cavities) and Stang (supramolecular coordination complexes, directional bonding) each have a strong claim. Nitschke and Ward are also major contributors, so a three-person prize may leave out an influential figure.
assessment.maturity: Well established, widely reproduced and followed by extensive applications. Recognition is timely, although the 2025 prize for metal-organic frameworks, and the earlier supramolecular prize of 1987, mean the committee may view this as adjacent to recently honoured territory.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 MOF prize and the earlier 1987 supramolecular prize
Credit among Fujita, Raymond, Stang, Nitschke and Ward
Applications beyond fundamental host-guest chemistry are still emerging

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers, especially alkanethiols on gold, are a model of molecular self-organisation at interfaces, and soft lithography translated them into a toolbox for patterning and for wetting, adhesion and biointerface control. SAMs underpin much of surface and colloid science, and I regard this as a cornerstone of interfacial physical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara (1983) reported the alkanethiol-on-gold monolayers, Whitesides developed the broad SAM and soft-lithography programme, and Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers are a priority question. Xia also contributed to soft lithography. Priority and the split between SAM fundamentals and the lithographic applications make the allocation delicate.
assessment.maturity: Mature and validated through decades of use, with very broad use in biosensing, electronics and surface science. If anything, recognition may be late, and some of the work has been absorbed into textbook knowledge.
uncertainties: Priority involving Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers
Allocation between the SAM discovery and soft-lithography applications
Whitesides's age and the question of whether the prize is still feasible

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns small molecules into inducers of proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, which gives a genuinely new chemical modality and a mechanistic explanation for the action of thalidomide-like drugs. It has opened undruggable targets and led to many clinical candidates, and the induced-proximity concept is an elegant chemical principle.
assessment.attribution: Crews (PROTAC concept with Deshaies and Sakamoto), Handa (cereblon as the thalidomide target) and Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure and design) are decisive, but Deshaies, Sakamoto, Gray and Ito also have strong claims. The configuration is hard to fix at three people.
assessment.maturity: The concept is validated, and degraders are in late clinical trials, but so far there is no approved PROTAC drug, so the clinical proof of principle is still arriving. Recognition may be somewhat premature in my view.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet, so long-term impact is not yet established
Wide and contested credit among eight credited names
Division between PROTACs and molecular glue degraders

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins was shown with defined, modified redox proteins that tunnelling through the protein medium governs rates, with distance and driving-force dependence following Marcus-type theory. It links physical-chemical electron-transfer theory to biological function and has influenced thinking in bioenergetics and photosynthesis research.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler carried out the decisive, systematic experiments on ruthenium-modified proteins; the two-name list looks fair, but Marcus theory itself was already recognised in 1992 and other groups (Isied, Moser and Dutton, Beratan and Onuchic on theory) also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Long established and widely cited, with the physical picture stable, so maturity is high. The risk is that the recognition would be viewed as late and that the topic overlaps with earlier prizes (Marcus 1992, photosynthetic reaction centre 1988).
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier electron-transfer prizes
Credit relative to Moser, Dutton, Beratan and Onuchic
Gray's age and long-standing candidacy

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-molecule FRET gives distance information and dynamics for individual biomolecules, revealing heterogeneity and conformational transitions that ensemble averaging hides. It brought a physical-chemistry view of molecular dynamics into mainstream biophysics and chemistry, and is used to study folding, enzymes, nucleic acids and membrane proteins.
assessment.attribution: Ha and Weiss introduced and demonstrated single-pair FRET on freely diffusing and immobilised molecules in the 1990s. Selvin and Zhuang also made major contributions, but Zhuang's best-known work is in super-resolution imaging and may be better treated separately. I am not fully certain of the precise priority dates.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and ubiquitous in the lab. Single-molecule detection was already recognised in 2014 (super-resolution) and 2012 or earlier, so the committee might judge this as partially covered by earlier prizes, although smFRET itself has not been recognised.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2014 Chemistry prize on single-molecule methods
Credit among Ha, Weiss, Selvin and Zhuang
Not certain of exact priority details
